article_title: OpenBSD 8.0 Raises the amd64 Kernel Address Space to 512G, Adds arm64 Hibernate and Retires the loongson Port
summary: Approved with one correction: a quoted qwx(4) 802.11n line changes the source's tense; all other claims verified.

content_preview.title: OpenBSD 8.0 Raises the amd64 Kernel Address Space to 512G, Adds arm64 Hibernate and Retires the loongson Port
content_preview.summary: OpenBSD 8.0, released October 20, 2026, grows amd64 kernel virtual address space from 4G to 512G, adds arm64 hibernate and RISC-V vector support, and ends loongson support.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The OpenBSD project released version 8.0 on October 20, 2026, which its [release page](https://www.openbsd.org/80.html) describes as the "61st OpenBSD release." [LWN.net](https://lwn.net/Articles/1101536/) summarized the release as including "the addition of hibernate support for arm64, an increase in the kernel virtual address space for amd64 to 512GB, quite a few improvements for the qwx driver that supports Qualcomm WiFi 6 devices, and much more."

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-structured Briefing (449 words, within 300-800). Selects a representative set of items from the release page's partial list and covers the three headline items (amd64 KVA, arm64 hibernate, loongson retirement) accurately. Title and summary are no stronger than the sources: 'Retires' matches the page's 'Retired support for loongson architecture'; '512G' matches the page; LWN's own wording is '512GB' and the article quotes that form only inside the LWN quote.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (openbsd.org/80.html, 200, no suspicious_patterns) and source-1.html.gz (lwn.net/Articles/1101536/, 200, no suspicious_patterns) from disk, then re-fetched both live; live text matches snapshots. OpenBSD page verified verbatim: 'Released October 20, 2026. (61st OpenBSD release)'; 'This is a partial list of new features and systems included in OpenBSD 8.0.'; 'Raised the size of amd64 kernel virtual address space from 4G to 512G.' (what was raised: amd64 kernel virtual address space, 4G to 512G); 'pmap(9) direct map now placed at a random location.'; 'Sped up swap encryption by using AES cpu instructions.'; 'Increased kernel virtual address space on amd64 allows mapping more than 4GB of VRAM.'; arm64 'Added hibernate support.' (no platform/hardware list or caveat is given on the page; the article correctly adds none); riscv64 'Added kernel support for the 'V' vector extension.'; 'Switched sparc64 to LLVM toolchain.'; 'Retired support for loongson architecture (not working with Clang 22).' (exact word 'Retired', matches article and title; parenthetical reason omitted by the article, acceptable); getexecpath(3) line; 'Added MP support for up to 64 VCPUs per guest VM.'; x2apic guest support; Intel Arc A-Series (DG2/Alchemist) in inteldrm(4); Intel E610 in ix(4); libexpat 2.8.4 with CVE-2026-66046, CVE-2026-76641, CVE-2026-76957; 'Hardened syspatch(8) against malicious scripts.'; 'Stopped pax(1) extracting malicious archives outside the working directory.'; 'Removed current directory from default pkg_add(1) search path.'; packages amd64 13060, aarch64 12907; GCC 16.1.0, Go 1.27.1, LLVM/Clang 21.1.8 and 22.1.8, Firefox 157.0 and ESR 153.4.0. ONE DEFECT: the article quotes "Added 802.11n support to qwx(4)." but the page reads 'Add 802.11n support to qwx(4). Advertise HT capabilities and pass HT/QoS peer association.' (present/imperative tense, from the page's driver changes list). LWN brief verified verbatim: 'OpenBSD 8.0 has been released. There are many new features, including the addition of hibernate support for arm64, an increase in the kernel virtual address space for amd64 to 512GB, quite a few improvements for the qwx driver that supports Qualcomm WiFi 6 devices, and much more. See the full changelog for details.' Posted October 20, 2026 by jzb. The brief is fully public and readable without login (only comments carry subscriber labels); the attribution to LWN is accurate. Independent sources: 1 (LWN, a one-paragraph brief that restates the release announcement; it adds no independent analysis). Not an Analysis, so the 4-source/2-independent rule does not apply. Both body URLs are in article.sources and vice versa; no orphans. Allowlist: openbsd.org (www stripped) and lwn.net both listed by exact hostname.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, dates, names and attributions verified against raw text. The only defect is the tense of the qwx(4) quotation. The 'What We Don't Know' statements (no benchmarks, no system counts) hold for both sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, no editorializing and no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No earlier OpenBSD coverage in src/content/articles or article-meta (grep for 'openbsd' finds only unrelated articles mentioning other topics). New topic.
concerns: Quoted fragment 'Added 802.11n support to qwx(4).' does not match the source's 'Add 802.11n support to qwx(4).' (tense altered inside quote marks); filed as a clarification-level correction.
Only one independent source, and it is a one-paragraph brief; acceptable for a Briefing of a release announcement.
recommendations: Quote release-page lines exactly, including tense, or paraphrase outside quote marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped release Briefing with a single minor misquotation covered by a corrections record. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate release coverage of a niche OS aimed at a defined systems-developer audience
